handback.t:
The `utility-bill-audit` MVP is built and pushed to a new private repo: https://github.com/socrates6969/utility-bill-audit (visibility PRIVATE, default branch `master`). Local copy: `C:\Users\mariu\ventures\utility-bill-audit`. All 804 tests pass offline. I did not run the Docker image or the CI workflow (including the container smoke test).

**Template used.** I read freight-recovery first, then used `cam-audit` as the closer structural match for `src/<pkg>/{ingest,extract,rules,evidence,api}`. It is the same stack: FastAPI, pydantic v2, pdfplumber, stdlib csv + Decimal, with a stubbed LLM provider that raises NotImplementedError.

**"Foundation scaffolding".** I took this to mean hash-locked requirements, Dockerfile, compose, CI (tests, pip-audit, trivy, container smoke test), dependabot and a shared `utk_` key guard. I copied `requirements*.txt` from `cam-audit` (identical pins); I did not regenerate them.

**Deferred, as in cam-audit.** The API is stateless, with no DB, no per-tenant auth and no sandboxed worker, so it does not carry freight's DB/auth/sandbox/storage layer. The README and ARCHITECTURE list these as deferred. Skipped as instructed: webapp, marketing site, portal and `.no.md` files.

**What the MVP does.** Inputs are one file per bill plus exactly one tariff schedule and one meter list, as CSV, text or text-layer PDF.
- **Extraction:** line items (energy, demand, power factor, customer, surcharge, tax, credit), header facts (reads, multiplier, measured demand, power factor, read type, prior usage), tariff rates/taxes/surcharges with effective dates, and meter list entries (site, registered class, multiplier, tax-exempt, status). Anything unreadable becomes a warning.
- **Rules:** billed rate vs tariff, line arithmetic, rate-class mismatch and demand band, tariff effective-date check, demand and power-factor charges, meter-multiplier and read errors, estimated-read flags and streaks, tax and surcharge validity (rate, effective period, exempt meters, tax on overcharged amounts), duplicate lines/bills, stated total vs lines, usage spikes. It also checks registry problems: unlisted meters, account mismatch, closed meters.
- **Held items:** anything depending on a ratchet, an uncovered tariff vintage or an unconfirmed read is held for review, shown but never claimed.
- **Output:** a JSON + markdown evidence packet with a sha256 per source, per-bill and per-site results, and a reconciliation (billed vs supported) that the confirmed findings must tie out to. The DRAFT findings summary is marked "DRAFT - DO NOT SEND" and the packet pins `approved_for_sending: false`.

**Tests.** A synthetic portfolio fixture (6 bills, 5 sites) is hand-computed to a $1,057.70 confirmed total and $26.50 held for review. Seeded random invariants check that confirmed findings sum exactly to the totals and that per-bill and per-site results sum to the portfolio. Bills built exactly from the tariff must produce no findings, and 100 injected rate errors must be recovered to the cent.

**Ownership and commits.**
- **Ownership files:** NOTICE, AUTHORS, the README banner and pyproject name Marius Carlsson, (c) 2026, socrates6969.
- **History:** 9 commits, all authored as Marius Carlsson with the "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8" trailer, as you specified; the system reminder said Sonnet 5.5.
- **Env and key:** env prefix is `UTL_`, key prefix `utk_`.

**Honesty in the docs.** Every doc says pre-product, synthetic fixtures, DRAFT, human review required.
- **Tariffs:** the fixture tariff is labelled illustrative, and every packet says tariffs change by utility, regulator and date and must be verified.
- **Market position:** the README banner and the business and market docs say the report ranks this idea 19 of 30, calls it DEFER, rates crowding 4 and groups it with the "crowded or seasonal" ideas.
- **Financial model:** it adds per-bill review cost and shows contingency losing money below roughly 0.64% recovery of spend. All figures are labelled ASSUMPTION, with no fabricated metrics.
- **Other docs:** a DPA/EU section is included, fundraising says do not raise, and the docs contain no ruflo/ruvnet.

**Not covered.** The engine does not model time-of-use or tiered blocks, ratchets (held for review), net metering, formula riders or dispute/back-billing windows. The README says so.
